choices.content: They are collinear only when their initial points are the same
They are collinear because their directions are opposite

solutions.explanation: There is no real number \(\lambda\) such that \((0,1)=\lambda(1,0)\), because the first coordinate would force \(\lambda=0\), while the second coordinate is 1.
solutions.title: Test for a scalar multiple

solutions.explanation: The ordered pairs represent vectors. Place both vectors at the origin: \((1,0)\) points along the positive \(x\)-axis, while \((0,1)\) points along the positive \(y\)-axis. These axes are perpendicular, so the vectors have neither the same nor opposite directions. Therefore they are not collinear, choice D.
